narration: The dataset is structurally usable (1200 rows x 24 columns, mixed numeric/categorical/boolean/datetime, clean binary target with 68.9/31.1 balance) but not ready to train as-is. Two issues block readiness. First, missingness: every column except credit_score, page_views, is_active, signup_date and target has missing values, ranging from 1.4% (monthly_spend) to 22.1% (industry), with 4 columns in the 10-50% band flagged by the profiler (language 19.5%, industry 22.1%, payment_method 13.9%, acquisition_channel 12.7%) and several near 8-9% (referral_count 8.6%, balance 8.5%, support_tickets 8.3%, device_type 8.3%). This needs an explicit imputation/drop strategy for both numeric and categorical features. Second, balance, session_minutes and discount_rate each have max 9999.0 with std ~825-846 vs. their IQR spread of only ~16-17 units in the central 50% and intermediate outlier counts (iqr_count 15, z_score_count 8 each) — a classic sentinel-value pattern that will distort scaling and any distance- or gradient-based model. Fixing sentinels/outliers plus a coherent imputation plan should make this trainable; the class imbalance also warrants stratified splitting and class weighting.

Verdict: needs_cleaning. The dataset is structurally usable (1,200 rows, 24 columns, a clean binary target with no missing values and a 69/31 class split), but three issues must be fixed before training.

1) Sentinel values masquerading as outliers. balance, session_minutes, and discount_rate each have max = 9999.0 while their q75 values are only 63.2, 66.6, and 70.1 respectively. The means (126.7, 127.4, 130.7) are pulled far above the medians (~54-62), and std (846, 828, 825) is ~70x the interquartile range. That is a classic 9999 sentinel/bad-value pattern, not real extreme observations. These must be recoded to missing or dropped, otherwise any scaler or tree split will be distorted.

2) Missing data. Four columns exceed the 10% warning threshold: industry (22.1%), language (19.5%), payment_method (13.9%), and acquisition_channel (12.7%). High-cardinality categoricals with 13-22% missing are the hardest to impute credibly; imputing industry with 31 levels is essentially guesswork. Numeric columns are mostly light (0-8.6%), so mean/median imputation plus missingness indicators would be reasonable there.

3) Categorical encoding. Cardinality is high and uneven: industry (31), language (27), payment_method (23), acquisition_channel (19), device_type (15), plan_tier (11), region (7). With only 1,200 rows, one-hot encoding all of these will produce a very wide, sparse matrix and invite overfitting; target/ordinal encoding or grouping rare levels is advisable.

Note also that the three sentinel-affected columns overlap heavily with the high-outlier columns (8 IQR/z-count outliers each), so the outlier counts reported are likely inflated by the sentinels. The dataset is otherwise well-formed (credit_score, page_views, is_active, signup_date, and target have 0% missing), so a moderate cleaning pass - recode sentinels, impute/indicate missing values, and control categorical cardinality - should make it trainable.
